chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) cut off a man's hand for theft of a 'baydah'. I asked: 'Which baydah?' He said: 'A baydah of iron, valued at one-third of a dinar.' I said: 'This is the lowest threshold for the thief's hand-cutting.' He remained silent.

key_terms.أَدْنَى حَدِّ: The lowest threshold or minimum limit.
key_terms.السَّارِقِ: The thief, subject to the punishment of hand-cutting.
key_terms.بَيضَة: A specific unit of weight or measure, here referring to a quantity of goods.
key_terms.بَيضَةُ حَدِيدٍ: A baydah of iron, specified as the minimum threshold for the punishment.
key_terms.ثُلُثُ دِينَارٍ: One-third of a dinar, the monetary value of the minimum threshold.

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for hand-cutting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the nisab (minimum value) for hadd al-sariqah by citing the precedent of Imam Ali cutting the hand of a thief who stole an iron egg worth one-third of a dinar. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the physical object (baydah) and its monetary valuation, establishing a concrete baseline for the severity of the punishment in Shia jurisprudence.
